results.title: Revolut to reduce hiring after AI automation campaign
results.author: Samuel Norman
highlights:
Nik Storonsky founded Revolut in 2015.

The billionaire founder of Revolut said the fintech is aiming to reduce hiring after leveraging AI for automation across the business.

Nik Storonsky, chief executive of the digital banking giant, told the Cheeky Pint podcast that the group began using AI to “optimise customer support” around two years ago.

He said now it was in “almost every single area of the company” and the company was “trying to create an AI employee end to end”.

“Technically one person can accomplish much more now… you can have one person doing all aspects of the product,” Storonsky said, but added the size of teams at Revolut have not changed yet.

“We’re just trying to automate a lot of things… hopefully when automation is done we can start hiring less people,” he said.

results.title: Revolut Reaches $115B Valuation Amid Performance-Driven Staff Reductions And AI Efficiency Push | Crowdfund Insider
results.author: Omar Faridi
highlights:
Even as the valuation soared and thousands of employees reportedly realized gains by selling stock, Revolut has begun reducing headcount through performance reviews.

Reports indicate dozens of staff—primarily in the Revolut Business unit serving small and medium-sized enterprises, and involving sales roles in the UK and other European offices—are departing.

A company spokesperson stated that the exits align with routine quarterly performance assessments seen in prior periods and do not constitute a formal layoff program.

With roughly 15,000 employees overall, the scale remains limited relative to the workforce, yet it coincides with the firm’s emphasis on operational discipline.

This staffing approach fits Revolut’s intensifying focus on artificial intelligence as a lever for productivity and cost control.

How is Revolut workforce data collected?

Observed profile trends use the latest available monthly professional profile snapshot. Company-reported workforce totals appear separately and only when supported by a primary company source or regulatory filing. Geography uses location information from individual profiles, aggregated separately from verified company headquarters. Data may lag internal company changes.

Methodology

The observed profile metric and trend chart use the same latest available monthly snapshot, with its observation month shown separately from the page update date. Company-reported workforce totals appear only when supported by a primary source and remain separate from profile counts. Geographic distributions use a separate current profile population and person location fields, never company headquarters. Country counts describe countries represented in those profiles, not offices. Location percentages include profiles without a known city or region in their denominator. Department, seniority, and title coverage may differ from the company workforce.
